title: TPA overview (cloud)
description: Home: is anything wrong now, by area, service and database (its backups and point-in-time logs too), read from Cloud Monitoring; the detail (each problem by name, uptime by host, the scheduled runs, each area's numbers) in the rows shut below. panels.title: Right now: each area, uptime, the sign-in journeys, incidents
Portal & sign-in
panels.description: The last 15 minutes in this project: how many problems, of 5xx answers, uptime and inside checks failing (beta's checks pass on IAP's sign-in page), synthetic journeys failed or broken, crashes, out-of-memory kills, failed job runs, minutes the database was down, its failed backups and failed point-in-time log archives, and five minutes or more with no instance for a service kept warm (auth-outbox-publisher, auth, tpa-api: `<service> has no instance` pages, urgent). Each one, named with its count, is in the shut row What's wrong now (details) below, and on Portal & API and Sign-in. A backup missing (its alert judges today's backup from 14:00 UTC) or point-in-time logs stalled for 30 minutes cannot be read in fifteen minutes: auth-db's backups and logs tiles (Databases, and What's wrong now) show them. Amber: something to look at; whether it paged is PagerDuty's (the Incidents tile). "? Can't tell": nothing arrived, or the query failed. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: now: the hosts as their outage policy reads them (each checker region's latest result over twenty minutes, the regions failing counted): ✕ down, red, when more than 1 region fails on any host, as `outage: <host>` pages; one region failing alone does not page. 24 h: the worst host's share of checks passed in the last 24 hours (each host's is in the shut row Right now (details), and over time on Portal & API). @@E@@Each check reads `/health` on a public host (the portal, auth and api hosts) from three US regions: a pass is the service answering through the load balancer and Cloud Armor. An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@Beta's hosts are behind IAP, so a check passes only on Google's sign-in page: it proves the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor and IAP, never the service behind them (that is the 5xx and instance panels). An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@

panels.title: Sign-in journeys (1 h)
panels.description: Each journey's runs in the last hour, by outcome (`synthetic_results`, one result line per run): `synthetics-staff-sign-in` (J1 staff sign-in): the portal, auth and a desk read that reaches tpa-db; `synthetics-ops-desk` (J2 ops desk): the ops host, auth and the live queue in svc-ops; `synthetics-crm` (J3 CRM sign-in): the CRM's own sign-in. pass is teal; fail is amber, red from two (`synthetic-failing` pages on two fails and no pass in eleven minutes; J1 and J2 urgent); error is amber (the runner itself broke: `synthetic-broken`). No runs at all: the journeys are off or paused (`synthetic-blind` when one goes quiet 15 minutes).

panels.title: Incidents

panels.title: auth-db backups (30 h)
panels.description: auth-db's successful automated backups in the last 30 hours (`sql_automated_backups`, windowStatus STATUS_SUCCEEDED) and its failed ones (`sql_backup_failures`). The alert, `auth-db-backup-missing` (urgent), judges today's backup, from 14:00 UTC: the window from 09:00 UTC closed an hour before with no successful backup while the instance was up all day. This tile shows a successful backup in the last 30 hours, so a missed night turns it red about two hours after the page (30 hours after the night before's backup). One backup a night, starting in a four-hour window from 09:00 UTC: on beta two land up to 26.1 hours apart, so a healthy instance always has one in 30 hours. ✕ none in 30 h, red: none while auth-db reported for 29 of the 30 hours or more; an instance started since reads "no backup yet". ✕ a backup failed, red: its newest failure (`auth-db-backup-failed`) is later than its newest success, each by the hour, so a failed attempt that a later attempt made good reads ✓ backed up, and a night that failed reads ✕ at once. The failed count, red from one, counts every failed entry in the 30 hours: one bad night writes several failed attempts and a final failure, so it is entries, not nights. ✓ backed up. Point-in-time recovery replays its seven days of logs from a backup taken before the minute chosen. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

One backup a night, starting in a four-hour window from 09:00 UTC: on beta two land up to 26.1 hours apart, so a healthy instance always has one in 30 hours. ✕ none in 30 h, red: none while crm-db reported for 29 of the 30 hours or more; an instance started since reads "no backup yet". ✕ a backup failed, red: its newest failure (`crm-db-backup-failed`) is later than its newest success, each by the hour, so a failed attempt that a later attempt made good reads ✓ backed up, and a night that failed reads ✕ at once. The failed count, red from one, counts every failed entry in the 30 hours: one bad night writes several failed attempts and a final failure, so it is entries, not nights. ✓ backed up. Point-in-time recovery replays its seven days of logs from a backup taken before the minute chosen. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `crm-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).
